answer: Metered bandwidth rewards pay for verified delivery, not account count. Agents serving juniper imagery, vine surveys and karst maps receive fresh random payloads to upload to independent test receivers. A verifier counts each nonce-bound payload once and caps payment at the measured byte rate. Splitting one connection among N accounts leaves its total throughput unchanged; N full-rate streams require N times the bandwidth, which the attacker must buy. This assumes honest receivers; colluding endpoints could falsely acknowledge traffic.
